assumptions: Subdomain node of evidence_synthesis_and_systematic_review; scope limited to review METHODS (finding/selecting/documenting evidence), not statistical meta-analysis modeling.
No observed dataset supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors from established methods literature.
Health/clinical conventions (PROSPERO, PRISMA 2020, RoB2/ROBINS-I, PRESS) are used as canonical exemplars while remaining discipline-general.
Each node is bounded to one high-effort reasoning session and produces a reusable handoff artifact.
exclusions: statistical meta-analysis estimation, heterogeneity, and pooling models
GRADE certainty-of-evidence rating mechanics (referenced only as appraisal consumers)
primary study conduct and primary data collection
qualitative synthesis coding methods beyond data extraction scope

competency_questions.question: Given a review objective, how is it operationalized into a structured, registrable question?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROTOCOL_REG and QUESTION_FRAME structure and register the question

competency_questions.question: Which review type (systematic, scoping, rapid, umbrella, realist) fits a given question and resources?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REVIEW_TYPOLOGY maps question and resources to a type

competency_questions.question: How are inclusion/exclusion criteria derived from the question's concepts?
How is each excluded study assigned a single reproducible exclusion reason?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ELIGIBILITY's taxonomy and FT_SCREEN's coded reasons

competency_questions.question: Which databases and sources are needed to cover the topic without systematic gaps?
How is a reproducible search strategy with controlled vocabulary and grey sources built?
How is the sensitivity-vs-precision tradeoff calibrated and the search verified before running?
How are records deduplicated and managed with preserved provenance and an audit trail?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEDUP and REF_MGMT preserve provenance and counts

competency_questions.question: How is screening performed (title/abstract, dual, optionally ML-assisted) to control selection bias?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TA_SCREEN, DUAL_SCREEN, SCREEN_AUTOMATION with recall control

competency_questions.question: How is every record accounted for from identification to inclusion in a PRISMA flow?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRISMA_FLOW reconciles counts from DEDUP and screening

competency_questions.question: How are screening conflicts between reviewers reconciled defensibly?
How are study data extracted and coded reproducibly from included studies?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DATA_EXTRACTION uses a piloted, dual-coded form

competency_questions.question: How is methodological quality (risk of bias) appraised with design-appropriate tools?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RISK_OF_BIAS applies a tool matched to each design

competency_questions.question: How is the review reported, made reproducible, and maintained as a living document?

glossary.definition: a review using explicit, reproducible methods to identify, appraise, and synthesize all relevant studies
an international prospective register of systematic review protocols
a framework structuring a question by population, intervention/exposure, comparator, and outcome
the operational inclusion and exclusion rules that gate study selection
standardized index terms such as MeSH or Emtree used in searching
evidence outside commercial publishing: registries, theses, preprints, reports
the proportion of relevant records a search retrieves
the proportion of retrieved records that are relevant
synonyms: positive predictive value of a search

glossary.definition: removing duplicate records of the same report across sources
independent screening by two reviewers with conflict reconciliation
the reporting standard and flow diagram for systematic reviews
a review continually updated as new evidence emerges, with versioned conclusions

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established systematic-review methods literature (Higgins et al., Cochrane Handbook 2019; Gough, Oliver & Thomas 2017; PRISMA 2020; PRESS) and methodological practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Draft, register, and version the review protocol (objectives, eligibility, methods, analysis plan) before screening begins, typically in PROSPERO.
contradictors: researcher who finalizes methods after seeing results

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when scope, question, or eligibility materially change after registration

pros.claim: locks methods a priori to curb selective reporting and HARKing
pros.example: registering a PICO and analysis plan before screening prevents post hoc criterion changes

pros.claim: creates a citable audit anchor and reduces duplicate reviews
pros.example: a PROSPERO ID lets others find the in-progress review

cons.claim: amendments are common and must be transparently logged, adding overhead
cons.example: an unforeseen subgroup requires a documented protocol amendment

cons.claim: premature registration of a vague protocol can mislead
cons.example: registering before the question is stable invites repeated amendments

failure_modes: vague eligibility that cannot gate inclusion
acceptance_tests: protocol contains objectives, eligibility, search, screening, extraction, and analysis sections
registry ID issued before title/abstract screening
every method change has a dated amendment entry

nodes.definition: Select the review type (systematic, scoping, rapid, umbrella, realist) whose method matches the question, evidence base, and resource constraints.
contradictors: author who labels a scoping review 'systematic' for prestige

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when timeline shrinks (rapid) or the question shifts from breadth to effect estimation

pros.claim: the review type fixes which methods and reporting standards apply
pros.example: a broad 'what is known' question maps to a scoping review, not a meta-analysis

pros.claim: prevents mismatch between question and synthesis logic
pros.example: an umbrella review answers 'what do existing reviews conclude'

cons.claim: rapid-review shortcuts trade comprehensiveness for speed and must be disclosed
cons.example: single-screener rapid review accepts higher miss risk

cons.claim: type boundaries blur and are sometimes mislabeled
cons.example: a 'systematic' label on a non-exhaustive search overstates rigor

failure_modes: type chosen for prestige not fit
scoping review forced into effect pooling
acceptance_tests: declared type matches the question's intent
reporting standard chosen matches the type

nodes.definition: Operationalize the review question into a structured framework (PICO/PECO/PCC) so eligibility and search terms are derivable from explicit concepts.
contradictors: author who searches before defining concepts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a core concept (population, exposure, or outcome) is redefined

pros.claim: explicit concepts make eligibility and search terms reproducible
pros.example: PICO concepts map directly to search blocks and inclusion rules

pros.claim: a prespecified outcome hierarchy curbs outcome switching
pros.example: primary vs secondary outcomes fixed before extraction

cons.claim: rigid frameworks fit poorly to qualitative or complex questions
cons.example: a realist question needs context-mechanism-outcome, not PICO

cons.claim: over-narrow framing can exclude relevant evidence
cons.example: tight comparator definition drops informative single-arm studies

acceptance_tests: each concept block has explicit terms
outcomes ranked primary/secondary a priori
framework matches question type

nodes.definition: Specify operational inclusion and exclusion criteria (population, design, outcomes, language, dates) that deterministically gate study selection.
contradictors: screener applying undocumented criteria

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a criterion is added, dropped, or reinterpreted during screening

pros.claim: deterministic criteria make screening reproducible and arbitrable
pros.example: two screeners reach the same include/exclude given the same rule set

pros.claim: a fixed exclusion-reason taxonomy feeds the PRISMA flow
pros.example: each full-text exclusion is tagged with a single coded reason

cons.claim: borderline studies expose criterion ambiguity
cons.example: a study with a partial population match forces a judgment call

cons.claim: language/date limits introduce selection bias if unjustified
cons.example: English-only restriction may miss relevant trials

acceptance_tests: each criterion is operational and testable
exclusion reasons map to a closed taxonomy
limits (date/language) are justified

nodes.definition: Construct the bibliographic search strategy: concept blocks, controlled vocabulary (MeSH/Emtree), free-text synonyms, Boolean/proximity operators, and validated filters.
contradictors: author using a single keyword string in one engine

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a missed seminal study reveals a synonym or vocabulary gap

pros.claim: concept-block logic with controlled vocabulary maximizes recall of relevant records
pros.example: MeSH plus free-text synonyms catch indexed and unindexed records

pros.claim: a line-by-line strategy is auditable and re-runnable
pros.example: each numbered search line can be reproduced exactly

cons.claim: complex Boolean logic is error-prone and database-specific
cons.example: an operator that works in Ovid fails in PubMed syntax

cons.claim: over-broad strategies explode screening load
cons.example: missing study-design filters returns tens of thousands of irrelevant hits

acceptance_tests: strategy reproduces a set of known relevant 'seed' records
each concept block documented line by line
syntax validated per database

nodes.definition: Select the set of bibliographic databases and platforms whose coverage spans the topic's disciplines, minimizing systematic gaps.
contradictors: reviewer relying on a single database

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the topic spans a discipline not covered by the current source list

pros.claim: multi-database coverage reduces discipline-specific retrieval gaps
pros.example: adding Embase and CINAHL complements MEDLINE for health topics

pros.claim: documented coverage justifies comprehensiveness claims
pros.example: listing why each database was chosen supports the methods section

cons.claim: more databases multiply duplicate records and screening cost
cons.example: a fourth database adds 30% records but few uniques

cons.claim: paywalled databases create access-dependent reproducibility
cons.example: reviewers without subscriptions cannot replicate

acceptance_tests: source list covers all in-scope disciplines
each source choice has a documented reason
revisit_triggers: access lost to a key database

nodes.definition: Search beyond databases (trial registries, theses, preprints, reports, reference checking, citation chasing, expert contact) to reduce publication and indexing bias.
contradictors: reviewer who searches only indexed journals

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when results show evidence of unpublished or unindexed studies

pros.claim: reduces publication and indexing bias by capturing unpublished/ongoing studies
pros.example: trial-registry search finds completed-but-unpublished trials

pros.claim: citation chasing recovers studies missed by term-based search
pros.example: backward/forward citation finds non-indexed relevant work

cons.claim: grey sources are heterogeneous and hard to document reproducibly
cons.example: handsearch and email contacts are not re-runnable

cons.claim: high effort with uncertain yield
cons.example: weeks of handsearching may add few includes

acceptance_tests: trial registries searched and documented
reference and citation chasing logged

nodes.definition: Calibrate the search to balance sensitivity (recall of relevant records) against precision (screening burden), making the tradeoff explicit and justified.
contradictors: reviewer who maximizes precision and silently loses recall

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when relative-recall checks show a known study was not retrieved

pros.claim: explicit recall priority protects against missing eligible studies
pros.example: systematic reviews favor sensitivity over precision by design

pros.claim: relative-recall checks quantify how complete the search is
pros.example: a seed set recovered estimates search sensitivity

cons.claim: high sensitivity inflates screening volume and cost
cons.example: a recall-maximizing search returns 90% irrelevant records

cons.claim: precision-favoring rapid reviews accept higher miss risk
cons.example: tightened filters trade completeness for speed

acceptance_tests: recall/precision balance is stated and justified
relative-recall check against a seed set performed

nodes.definition: Remove duplicate records across databases and sources using algorithmic and manual methods while avoiding erroneous removal of distinct studies.
contradictors: reviewer who trusts a single automatic dedup pass blindly

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when duplicate-removal errors are detected during screening

pros.claim: removing duplicates cuts screening burden and double-counting
pros.example: one record per study prevents double inclusion in synthesis

pros.claim: a recorded removed-count feeds the PRISMA flow accurately
pros.example: duplicates-removed number is required for the flow diagram

cons.claim: over-aggressive matching can delete distinct companion reports
cons.example: two reports of one trial vs two distinct trials confused

cons.claim: manual dedup is laborious for large sets
cons.example: tens of thousands of records strain manual review

acceptance_tests: dedup method documented and reproducible
removed-count recorded for PRISMA flow

nodes.definition: Configure reference-management/review software to ingest records, preserve provenance, deduplicate, and route records through screening with an audit trail.
contradictors: reviewer tracking screening in an ad hoc spreadsheet

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when tooling cannot preserve source provenance or audit state

pros.claim: centralized tooling preserves provenance and a re-runnable audit trail
pros.example: each record retains which database it came from

pros.claim: integrated screening tools support dual screening and conflict tracking
pros.example: two reviewers screen in parallel with hidden decisions

cons.claim: tool lock-in and import errors corrupt counts
cons.example: malformed RIS import drops fields silently

cons.claim: licensing and learning curve add overhead
cons.example: a paid tool may be inaccessible to all reviewers

acceptance_tests: every imported record retains source provenance
screening decisions are exportable as an audit log

nodes.definition: Screen titles and abstracts of deduplicated records against eligibility criteria to exclude clearly irrelevant records before full-text retrieval.
contradictors: single screener excluding aggressively at abstract stage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when calibration shows inconsistent application of a criterion

pros.claim: early exclusion of irrelevant records focuses full-text effort
pros.example: abstract screening removes obviously off-topic records cheaply

pros.claim: a liberal 'when in doubt, include' rule protects recall
pros.example: ambiguous abstracts pass to full text rather than being dropped

cons.claim: abstracts are incomplete and cause wrongful exclusion
cons.example: an informative study with a poor abstract is wrongly excluded

cons.claim: single-screener abstract exclusion risks missed includes
cons.example: one reviewer's bias drops a relevant record

acceptance_tests: a screening-calibration exercise was run before full screening
ambiguous records are advanced not excluded

nodes.definition: Retrieve and assess full texts of advanced records against all eligibility criteria, recording a single coded exclusion reason for each excluded study.
contradictors: reviewer excluding at full text without recording a reason

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an exclusion reason is found to be misapplied on re-check

pros.claim: full-text assessment yields the definitive included set
pros.example: criteria are applied to complete reports, not abstracts

pros.claim: coded exclusion reasons populate the PRISMA flow and are auditable
pros.example: each exclusion tagged with one reason from a fixed list

cons.claim: unretrievable full texts threaten completeness
cons.example: a key report behind a paywall cannot be assessed

cons.claim: full-text retrieval and reading is the costliest screening stage
cons.example: hundreds of full texts must be obtained and read

acceptance_tests: every full-text exclusion has exactly one coded reason
unretrievable reports are listed and counted

nodes.definition: Have two reviewers independently screen records, measure agreement, and reconcile conflicts via discussion or a third reviewer to reduce selection bias.
contradictors: team using a single screener to save time without disclosure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when inter-rater agreement falls below the prespecified threshold

pros.claim: independent double screening reduces single-reviewer selection bias
pros.example: two reviewers catch each other's missed includes

pros.claim: agreement metrics and adjudication make decisions defensible
pros.example: kappa plus a documented third-reviewer rule

cons.claim: doubles screening labor
cons.example: every record screened twice at both stages

cons.claim: reconciliation can entrench a dominant reviewer's view
cons.example: third-reviewer adjudication needed to break ties fairly

failure_modes: conflicts resolved by deference not criteria
acceptance_tests: records double-screened with conflicts reconciled
a third-reviewer/adjudication rule is defined

nodes.definition: Account for every record from identification through inclusion in a PRISMA flow diagram, with consistent counts at each stage.
contradictors: author whose flow numbers do not add up

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when stage counts fail to reconcile across the flow

pros.claim: a reconciled flow makes selection transparent and reproducible
pros.example: every record is traceable from identification to inclusion

pros.claim: PRISMA 2020 flow is expected by journals and reviewers
pros.example: reviewers check that numbers add up stage to stage

cons.claim: reconstructing counts retroactively is error-prone
cons.example: counts not logged in real time fail to balance

cons.claim: new-source updates complicate the flow
cons.example: a search update needs a revised flow diagram

acceptance_tests: identification minus duplicates minus exclusions equals the included count
each stage count is sourced and reconcilable

nodes.definition: Extract and code study characteristics, outcomes, and context into a piloted, structured form with dual extraction and verification for accuracy.
contradictors: single extractor with no verification

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a needed variable was not prespecified in the extraction form

pros.claim: a piloted, prespecified form yields consistent extractable data
pros.example: fields fixed before extraction prevent ad hoc additions

pros.claim: dual extraction with verification reduces transcription error
pros.example: two extractors reconcile discrepant values

cons.claim: extraction is labor-intensive and error-prone for complex outcomes
cons.example: multi-arm trials need careful arm-level coding

cons.claim: unreported data force assumptions or author contact
cons.example: missing standard deviations require imputation or queries

acceptance_tests: extraction form piloted on a sample of studies
extractions dual-coded and reconciled

nodes.definition: Apply a validated critical-appraisal/risk-of-bias tool to each included study, judging methodological quality at the study and outcome level.
contradictors: reviewer who pools all studies regardless of quality

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a more appropriate appraisal tool exists for the study designs

pros.claim: validated tools give defensible, domain-level quality judgments
pros.example: RoB2 assesses randomization, deviations, missing data, measurement, and selection

pros.claim: quality judgments inform sensitivity analyses and certainty grading
pros.example: high-risk studies can be down-weighted or excluded in sensitivity runs

cons.claim: appraisal is judgment-laden and tool-dependent
cons.example: two appraisers rate the same domain differently

cons.claim: the wrong tool for the design produces invalid ratings
cons.example: using a trial tool on observational studies misjudges bias

acceptance_tests: appraisal tool matches the included study designs
appraisals dual-rated and reconciled

nodes.definition: Report the completed review against the PRISMA 2020 checklist so methods and results are transparent, complete, and appraisable.
contradictors: author omitting the full search strategy from the report

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a checklist item is unmet or a reporting standard is updated

pros.claim: checklist-driven reporting makes the review reproducible and appraisable
pros.example: each PRISMA item maps to a manuscript location

pros.claim: publishing the full strategy and protocol link enables replication
pros.example: readers can re-run the documented search

cons.claim: checklist compliance does not guarantee methodological quality
cons.example: a complete checklist can still describe a weak search

cons.claim: reporting overhead is substantial for complex reviews
cons.example: mapping 27 items takes meaningful effort

acceptance_tests: all applicable PRISMA 2020 items are addressed and located
the full search strategy and registration are reported

nodes.definition: Have a second information specialist peer-review the search strategy (e.g., via PRESS) to catch errors in logic, syntax, vocabulary, and translation before running it.
contradictors: author who runs an unreviewed search

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when peer review finds a logic or syntax error in the strategy

pros.claim: a structured PRESS review catches Boolean and vocabulary errors before running
pros.example: a second specialist spots a missing synonym or misplaced operator

pros.claim: early correction avoids costly re-running and re-screening
pros.example: fixing the strategy before execution prevents missed records

cons.claim: requires a second qualified specialist
cons.example: small teams lack a second information specialist

cons.claim: adds a step before search execution
cons.example: peer review delays the start of retrieval

acceptance_tests: the search strategy passes a PRESS-style peer review with findings addressed

nodes.definition: Maintain a review as a living document with scheduled search re-runs, incremental screening, and versioned updates as new evidence emerges.
contradictors: author treating a fast-moving topic as a one-time review

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a search re-run yields new includes that change conclusions

pros.claim: keeps conclusions current in fast-moving fields
pros.example: monthly re-runs incorporate new trials as they publish

pros.claim: incremental updates are cheaper than full re-reviews
pros.example: only new records are screened each cycle

cons.claim: sustained effort and infrastructure are required
cons.example: living reviews demand ongoing reviewer and tooling commitment

cons.claim: version drift complicates citation of conclusions
cons.example: readers must know which version they cite

acceptance_tests: update cadence and triggers are defined
each update is versioned with an incremental flow

nodes.definition: Use machine-learning record prioritization and screening assistance to reduce screening burden while controlling and disclosing miss risk.
contradictors: reviewer who trusts auto-exclusion without recall validation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when validated recall at the chosen stopping point falls below target

pros.claim: prioritization surfaces relevant records early and cuts screening time
pros.example: active learning ranks likely-includes first

pros.claim: explicit stopping rules with recall estimates bound the miss risk
pros.example: stop screening at an estimated 95% recall with disclosure

cons.claim: auto-exclusion can silently drop eligible studies
cons.example: an unvalidated model excludes a relevant outlier

cons.claim: performance varies by topic and training quality
cons.example: sparse positive labels degrade the model

acceptance_tests: estimated recall at the stopping point is reported
automation use and its limits are disclosed

nodes.definition: Capture and preserve a complete, dated audit trail (full strings, dates, hit counts, source versions) so the entire retrieval is reproducible by a third party.
contradictors: author reporting only summary search terms

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a third party cannot reproduce the reported retrieval

pros.claim: a dated full-string log makes the search reproducible and verifiable
pros.example: another team can re-run the exact strings on the same platforms

pros.claim: recorded hit counts and dates support transparency and updates
pros.example: baseline counts enable incremental update accounting

cons.claim: platforms change, so historical re-runs may not match exactly
cons.example: a database update alters counts after the fact

cons.claim: capturing full logs adds documentation overhead
cons.example: every line and run date must be saved

acceptance_tests: full search strings, dates, and per-source counts are captured
an independent re-run reproduces the reported counts within drift tolerance

edges.why_related: the registered protocol fixes objectives the review type must serve
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing a type before the protocol leaves it ungrounded
edges.example: a protocol with effect-estimation aims implies a systematic review
edges.resolution_rule: settle protocol objectives before declaring the review type

edges.why_related: the protocol's objectives are the source material the question framework structures
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a structured question inherits protocol intent
edges.risk_of_conflict: framing without a protocol risks unanchored scope
edges.example: protocol aim becomes a PICO question
edges.resolution_rule: draft protocol objectives before structuring the question

edges.why_related: eligibility criteria are operationalized directly from the question's concepts
edges.risk_of_conflict: criteria not derived from concepts gate inconsistently
edges.example: PICO population becomes the population inclusion rule
edges.resolution_rule: define concepts before writing eligibility rules

edges.why_related: search concept blocks are built from the question's concepts
edges.risk_of_conflict: searching without concepts produces ad hoc terms
edges.example: each PICO concept becomes a Boolean block
edges.resolution_rule: fix concepts before authoring search blocks

edges.why_related: eligibility limits (design, dates) bound which filters the search applies
edges.risk_of_conflict: mismatch between filters and criteria distorts recall
edges.example: an RCT-only criterion adds a trial filter
edges.resolution_rule: keep filters consistent with eligibility limits

edges.why_related: eligibility scope determines which disciplines and thus databases are needed
edges.risk_of_conflict: scope-blind source choice leaves gaps
edges.example: a nursing scope adds CINAHL
edges.resolution_rule: set eligibility scope before fixing the source list

edges.why_related: the review type bounds how exhaustive the search must be
edges.risk_of_conflict: an exhaustive search forced on a rapid review wastes resources
edges.example: a rapid review caps databases and date range
edges.resolution_rule: let the declared type set search comprehensiveness

edges.why_related: a drafted strategy must exist before it can be peer-reviewed
edges.risk_of_conflict: reviewing nothing wastes the step
edges.example: PRESS review of the drafted strings
edges.resolution_rule: draft the strategy before requesting PRESS review

edges.why_related: peer-review findings trigger revision of the search strategy
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring findings leaves errors in the run
edges.example: a missing synonym flagged by review is added
edges.resolution_rule: revise the strategy until review findings are resolved; stop when sign-off is granted

edges.why_related: the drafted strategy is the object whose recall/precision is calibrated
edges.risk_of_conflict: calibrating nothing is impossible
edges.example: tighten filters after a draft over-returns
edges.resolution_rule: author the strategy before calibrating sensitivity

edges.why_related: calibration outcomes feed edits back into the strategy
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded retuning delays execution
edges.example: a failed recall check adds terms
edges.resolution_rule: retune until the recall check passes; stop after the calibrated target is met

edges.why_related: each database's syntax constrains how the strategy is expressed
edges.risk_of_conflict: one generic string fails across platforms
edges.example: Ovid vs PubMed syntax differs
edges.resolution_rule: translate the strategy per selected database

edges.why_related: primary search results reveal where supplementary searching is needed
edges.risk_of_conflict: unfocused grey search is inefficient
edges.example: reference chasing seeds from included studies
edges.resolution_rule: run the primary search before supplementary searching

edges.why_related: the source list determines what records the reference manager ingests
edges.risk_of_conflict: unconfigured tooling loses provenance
edges.example: each database export is imported with a source tag
edges.resolution_rule: fix the source list before configuring import

edges.why_related: executed search results are the raw input deduplication processes
edges.benefit_of_coupling: dedup acts on the full set
edges.risk_of_conflict: deduping a partial set miscounts
edges.example: combined exports are dedduped together
edges.resolution_rule: complete retrieval before deduplication

edges.why_related: supplementary records join the pool that is deduplicated
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping grey in dedup double-counts
edges.example: a registry hit duplicates a database record
edges.resolution_rule: include grey records in the dedup pool

edges.why_related: the reference manager is the environment in which deduplication runs
edges.risk_of_conflict: dedup outside tooling loses audit trail
edges.example: tool-based dedup with manual review
edges.resolution_rule: load records into tooling before deduplicating

edges.why_related: deduplicated records are the unit set fed into abstract screening
edges.risk_of_conflict: screening duplicates wastes effort and double-counts
edges.example: screen 4,000 unique records not 6,000 raw
edges.resolution_rule: deduplicate before title/abstract screening

edges.why_related: abstract screening applies the eligibility criteria
edges.risk_of_conflict: screening without criteria is arbitrary
edges.example: exclude off-population records by rule
edges.resolution_rule: finalize eligibility before screening

edges.why_related: records advanced at abstract stage are the input to full-text screening
edges.benefit_of_coupling: full text assesses only advanced records
edges.risk_of_conflict: full-texting everything is wasteful
edges.example: retrieve full text for 'maybe' records
edges.resolution_rule: complete abstract screening before full-text screening

edges.why_related: dual screening governs how each screening decision is made
edges.risk_of_conflict: single screening lets bias through
edges.example: two reviewers label each abstract
edges.resolution_rule: apply dual screening across the screening stages

edges.why_related: automation augments but must not silently replace human screening decisions
edges.risk_of_conflict: auto-exclusion can drop eligible studies
edges.example: active learning ranks records for a human
edges.resolution_rule: keep a validated human-in-the-loop recall check on any automation

edges.why_related: full-text screening applies the full eligibility criteria
edges.risk_of_conflict: criteria-free full-texting is unreproducible
edges.example: exclude by coded reason at full text
edges.resolution_rule: finalize eligibility before full-text screening

edges.why_related: the duplicates-removed count is a required input to the flow diagram
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing dedup count breaks the flow
edges.example: duplicates-removed feeds the flow box
edges.resolution_rule: record the dedup count for the flow

edges.why_related: abstract screening tallies populate the flow's screening stage
edges.risk_of_conflict: unrecorded tallies break reconciliation
edges.example: records screened/excluded feed the flow
edges.resolution_rule: log screening tallies for the flow

edges.why_related: full-text inclusions and coded exclusions populate the flow's final stages
edges.benefit_of_coupling: flow ends in the included count
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing exclusion reasons break the flow
edges.example: coded exclusions feed the flow
edges.resolution_rule: record full-text outcomes for the flow

edges.why_related: the final included-study set is the input to data extraction
edges.risk_of_conflict: extracting from a non-final set causes rework
edges.example: extract from the confirmed include list
edges.resolution_rule: finalize inclusion before extraction

edges.why_related: the outcome hierarchy fixes which variables the extraction form captures
edges.risk_of_conflict: unprespecified fields invite outcome switching
edges.example: primary outcomes become required fields
edges.resolution_rule: derive extraction fields from the question's outcomes

edges.why_related: extracted methods detail is the evidence the appraisal tool judges
edges.risk_of_conflict: appraising without method detail is unreliable
edges.example: randomization detail feeds RoB2
edges.resolution_rule: extract methods detail before appraising bias

edges.why_related: the completed flow diagram is a required element of PRISMA 2020 reporting
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing flow fails the checklist
edges.example: the flow diagram is a checklist item
edges.resolution_rule: complete the flow before final reporting

edges.why_related: risk-of-bias results are required content in the report
edges.risk_of_conflict: omitted appraisal fails reporting standards
edges.example: RoB summary appears in results
edges.resolution_rule: complete appraisal before reporting

edges.why_related: extracted study characteristics populate the reported results
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting without extraction is empty
edges.example: characteristics table comes from extraction
edges.resolution_rule: extract before reporting results

edges.why_related: registration and protocol details must be disclosed in the report
edges.risk_of_conflict: undisclosed registration is a reporting gap
edges.example: PROSPERO ID appears in methods
edges.resolution_rule: register before reporting, then disclose it

edges.why_related: the executed strategy is what the audit trail captures for reproducibility
edges.risk_of_conflict: an uncaptured search cannot be replicated
edges.example: full strings and dates are logged
edges.resolution_rule: capture the strategy as it is executed

edges.why_related: platform and version metadata for each source feed the audit trail
edges.risk_of_conflict: unrecorded platforms block replication
edges.example: record Ovid MEDLINE version and date
edges.resolution_rule: log source platforms and versions

edges.why_related: the audit trail supplies the publishable full search strategy
edges.risk_of_conflict: unaudited searches cannot be fully reported
edges.example: the logged strings become a supplement
edges.resolution_rule: maintain the audit trail to enable full reporting

edges.why_related: a completed reported review is the baseline a living review updates
edges.risk_of_conflict: updating before a baseline is incoherent
edges.example: version 1 becomes the living baseline
edges.resolution_rule: complete and report the baseline before living-review updates

edges.why_related: search sensitivity changes the volume of records flowing into screening counts
edges.risk_of_conflict: an undisclosed precision bias understates the search
edges.example: a recall-max search inflates identified records
edges.resolution_rule: disclose the calibration that drove the record volume

edges.why_related: appraisal can reveal that an additional methods variable must be extracted
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded back-and-forth delays synthesis
edges.example: RoB needs allocation-concealment detail not yet extracted
edges.resolution_rule: add the missing variable then re-extract; stop when appraisal has needed inputs

edges.why_related: dual screening also governs full-text decisions, not just abstracts
edges.risk_of_conflict: single full-text screening lets bias in
edges.example: two reviewers confirm each inclusion
edges.resolution_rule: extend dual screening to full-text decisions

conflict_axes.trigger: maximizing recall inflates the screening workload
resolution_order: state the review's recall priority
accept the screening load a systematic review requires
disclose any precision-favoring shortcuts
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for a full systematic review, sensitivity dominates and the screening burden is accepted; rapid reviews may favor precision with disclosure
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a recall-favoring search exceeds team screening capacity
conflict_axes.example: a recall-maximizing search returns 90% irrelevant records the team must screen

conflict_axes.trigger: deadlines pressure teams to drop dual screening or comprehensive search
resolution_order: declare the review type and its accepted shortcuts
preserve recall-critical steps
disclose every methodological concession
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: rigor dominates for systematic reviews; rapid reviews may relax steps only with explicit disclosure of the resulting miss risk
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if shortcuts are taken without disclosing them as rapid-review methods
conflict_axes.example: a team drops second-reviewer screening to meet a deadline without disclosure

conflict_axes.trigger: broad mapping questions conflict with narrow effect-estimation eligibility
resolution_order: identify whether the goal is mapping or effect estimation
match the review type to that goal
set eligibility breadth accordingly
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the question's intent dominates: mapping intent favors scoping breadth, effect-estimation intent favors systematic depth
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a scoping question is forced into a narrow pooled estimate
conflict_axes.example: a 'what is known about X' question wrongly narrowed to a single comparator

conflict_axes.trigger: auto-exclusion can drop eligible studies to save effort
resolution_order: set a target recall and stopping rule
validate recall before trusting auto-exclusion
disclose automation and its limits
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: recall assurance dominates: automation is allowed only with a validated recall estimate and disclosure; otherwise human screening governs
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if auto-exclusion is used without a validated recall estimate
conflict_axes.example: an ML model stops screening early and misses an eligible outlier

conflict_axes.trigger: grey and handsearching add coverage but are hard to document reproducibly
resolution_order: prioritize reproducible documentation of every source
capture grey-source steps as fully as possible
disclose non-reproducible steps explicitly
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reproducibility dominates the reporting claim: comprehensive grey searching is pursued but each step must be documented or its limits disclosed
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if grey-source steps cannot be documented and are not disclosed
conflict_axes.example: email-to-authors contacts that cannot be replicated by another team

conflict_axes.trigger: new evidence tempts unregistered changes to criteria or outcomes
resolution_order: compare any proposed change to the registered protocol
require a dated amendment for material changes
report all deviations transparently
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the a priori protocol dominates: changes are permitted only as logged, disclosed amendments, never silently
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if eligibility or outcomes change without a protocol amendment
conflict_axes.example: adding a subgroup outcome after seeing results without registering it

conflict_axes.trigger: adding sources improves coverage but multiplies duplicates and screening cost
resolution_order: estimate marginal unique yield of each source
prioritize sources covering uncovered disciplines
stop adding sources at diminishing unique yield
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: coverage of in-scope disciplines dominates until marginal unique yield is negligible, after which cost dominates
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a source adds large duplicate volume but few unique includes
conflict_axes.example: a fourth database adds 30% records but only a handful of uniques

conflict_axes.trigger: aggressive matching risks deleting distinct companion reports or studies
resolution_order: use conservative automatic matching
manually verify near-duplicate clusters
preserve companion reports linked to one study
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: preserving distinct studies dominates: when in doubt a record is kept and manually checked rather than auto-removed
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if automatic dedup removes records without manual verification of near-duplicates
conflict_axes.example: two reports of one trial merged with two distinct trials

conflict_axes.trigger: a complete checklist can coexist with a methodologically weak review
resolution_order: treat PRISMA as a transparency floor not a quality ceiling
run search peer review and risk-of-bias appraisal independently
report quality limitations alongside the checklist
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: methodological quality controls dominate the quality claim; the checklist governs only transparency, so both must be satisfied independently
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if checklist completeness is used to imply methodological rigor
conflict_axes.example: a fully checklist-compliant review built on an unreviewed, narrow search

edge_cases.trigger: eligibility or outcomes change after registration without an amendment
edge_cases.example: a new outcome is added after screening with no PROSPERO amendment
edge_cases.detection_method: diff the live methods against the registered protocol record
resolution: log a dated amendment
disclose the deviation in the report

edge_cases.trigger: search run against a single database only
edge_cases.failure_mode: systematic discipline coverage gap and missed eligible studies
edge_cases.example: a health-and-social-care review searches only MEDLINE
edge_cases.detection_method: check the source list covers every in-scope discipline
resolution: add discipline-appropriate databases
document coverage rationale

edge_cases.trigger: one search string reused across platforms without syntax translation
edge_cases.failure_mode: silent zero/low hits on platforms where the syntax is invalid
edge_cases.example: PubMed bracket syntax fails when pasted into Ovid
edge_cases.detection_method: compare per-database hit counts for implausible drops
resolution: translate operators and field tags per platform
re-run and re-log counts

edge_cases.trigger: the strategy fails to retrieve a known relevant seed study
edge_cases.failure_mode: low search sensitivity and missed eligible records
edge_cases.example: a landmark trial is not returned by the draft strategy
edge_cases.detection_method: run a relative-recall check against a curated seed set
resolution: add the missing synonym or vocabulary term
re-run and re-check recall

edge_cases.trigger: automatic deduplication removes distinct studies as duplicates
edge_cases.failure_mode: loss of eligible studies and undercounted evidence
edge_cases.example: two same-author trials in the same year auto-merged
edge_cases.detection_method: audit a sample of auto-removed records for distinct studies
resolution: use conservative matching
manually verify near-duplicate clusters

edge_cases.failure_mode: single-reviewer selection bias and missed includes
edge_cases.example: one reviewer screens all abstracts to save time, undisclosed
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether decisions are double-screened and agreement is reported
resolution: add a second screener for a sample or all records
report the screening method honestly

edge_cases.trigger: full-text exclusions recorded without coded reasons
edge_cases.failure_mode: non-reproducible selection and a broken PRISMA flow
edge_cases.example: a study is excluded with no reason tagged
edge_cases.detection_method: check every full-text exclusion has exactly one coded reason
resolution: assign a coded reason to each exclusion
reconcile the flow tallies

edge_cases.trigger: PRISMA flow stage counts do not add up
edge_cases.example: screened minus excluded does not equal full-text assessed
edge_cases.detection_method: verify identification minus duplicates minus exclusions equals included
resolution: recount each stage from the audit log
correct the flow diagram

edge_cases.trigger: ML auto-exclusion used without a validated recall estimate
edge_cases.example: screening stopped early by a model with no recall check
edge_cases.detection_method: require a reported, validated recall at the stopping point
resolution: validate recall on a labeled holdout
disclose automation and stop only above the recall target

edge_cases.trigger: a risk-of-bias tool is applied to an incompatible study design
edge_cases.example: RoB2 applied to non-randomized observational studies
edge_cases.detection_method: check the appraisal tool matches each included design
resolution: select the design-appropriate tool
re-appraise affected studies

edge_cases.trigger: only summary terms reported instead of full dated strings
edge_cases.failure_mode: the search cannot be reproduced or updated
edge_cases.example: a methods section lists keywords but not the executable strings
edge_cases.detection_method: check that full strings, dates, and per-source counts are published
resolution: publish the complete strategy as a supplement
record run dates and platform versions

edge_cases.trigger: a living review's updates stop or lose version control
edge_cases.example: a living review's last update is two years stale but cited as current
edge_cases.detection_method: check update cadence adherence and version tags on conclusions
resolution: resume the update cadence or set a retirement decision
version every update with an incremental flow

workflow.objective: register the protocol, choose the review type, and structure the question a priori
acceptance_tests: protocol covers all required sections
registry ID issued before screening
question concepts are explicit
workflow.do_first_because: the a priori protocol is the highest-coupling foundation every later step inherits

workflow.objective: operationalize inclusion and exclusion criteria from the structured question
acceptance_tests: each criterion is operational and testable
exclusion reasons form a closed taxonomy
workflow.do_first_because: eligibility gates every screening decision and must precede search and screening

workflow.objective: design, calibrate, and peer-review the search strategy and source list
acceptance_tests: strategy recovers the seed set
strategy passes PRESS review
recall/precision balance justified
workflow.do_first_because: a reviewed, calibrated search prevents costly missed-study rework after screening

workflow.objective: execute the search, add grey sources, import to tooling, deduplicate, and capture the audit trail
acceptance_tests: dedup method documented and removed-count recorded
full strings, dates, and counts captured
workflow.do_first_because: capturing provenance and counts now prevents an unreproducible search and a broken flow later

workflow.objective: dual-screen titles and abstracts against eligibility, with optional validated automation
acceptance_tests: calibration exercise completed before full screening
any automation reports a validated recall
exit_criteria: abstract screening complete with conflicts reconciled
workflow.do_first_because: calibrated dual screening early prevents re-screening after criterion drift

workflow.objective: retrieve and dual-screen full texts, recording one coded exclusion reason per exclusion
entry_criteria: abstract screening complete with conflicts reconciled
acceptance_tests: every full-text exclusion has one coded reason
unretrievable reports listed
workflow.do_first_because: a confirmed final set prevents extraction rework on later-excluded studies

workflow.objective: reconcile counts across all stages into a PRISMA flow diagram
acceptance_tests: identification minus duplicates minus exclusions equals included
each count is sourced
workflow.do_first_because: reconciling counts now avoids retroactive count reconstruction errors at reporting

workflow.objective: extract data on a piloted form and appraise risk of bias with validated tools
acceptance_tests: extraction form piloted and dual-coded
appraisal tool matches each design
workflow.do_first_because: piloting and dual coding prevent re-extraction when fields or tools prove unfit

workflow.objective: report the review against the PRISMA 2020 checklist with full transparency
acceptance_tests: all applicable PRISMA items addressed and located
full search strategy and registration reported
exit_criteria: report passes the checklist and human review
workflow.do_first_because: checklist-driven reporting before any hard lock ensures the review is appraisable and reproducible

workflow.objective: decide on and operate a living-review update cycle for fast-moving topics
entry_criteria: report passes the checklist and human review
acceptance_tests: update cadence and triggers defined
each update versioned with an incremental flow
exit_criteria: living-review cycle defined or review retired
workflow.do_first_because: deciding maintenance after a stable baseline prevents premature or stale updates

priority_rationale.notes: a priori root every step inherits
type fixes methods and reporting standard
capture audit trail as search runs
one record per study before screening
optional burden reduction with recall control
quality judgments for synthesis and report

dominance_rules.trigger: a deadline pressures dropping a recall-critical or bias-control step
dominance_rules.rule: rigor dominates speed for systematic reviews; only declared rapid reviews may relax steps with disclosure
dominance_rules.required_action: preserve dual screening and comprehensive search, or re-declare as a rapid review with disclosed limits
dominance_rules.example: a team skips the second screener to meet a deadline without disclosure

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value step is tempting to start before its prerequisite is finalized
dominance_rules.required_action: block the dependent step until its prerequisite passes its gate
dominance_rules.example: starting extraction before the included set is final

dominance_rules.trigger: a numeric estimate looks confident but lacks a supporting source
dominance_rules.required_action: keep the heuristic label and source ref; do not present unsupported numbers as observed
dominance_rules.example: labeling a heuristic recall estimate as observed without data

dominance_rules.rule: for systematic reviews, recall dominates screening convenience
dominance_rules.required_action: accept the screening load or disclose any precision-favoring shortcut as a rapid-review method
dominance_rules.example: tightening filters to cut screening at the cost of recall

dominance_rules.trigger: screening automation could replace a human recall check
dominance_rules.rule: validated human-in-the-loop recall assurance dominates full automation
dominance_rules.required_action: require a validated recall estimate and disclosure before trusting auto-exclusion
dominance_rules.example: stopping screening on a model with no recall validation

dominance_rules.trigger: new evidence tempts an unregistered change to criteria or outcomes
dominance_rules.rule: the registered protocol dominates emergent convenience
dominance_rules.required_action: make the change only as a dated, disclosed amendment
dominance_rules.example: adding a subgroup outcome post hoc without amending PROSPERO

dominance_rules.trigger: a step is ready to lock before its acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.required_action: do not lock until acceptance tests and gates pass
dominance_rules.example: locking the search before PRESS findings are addressed

dominance_rules.trigger: there is pressure to add many records or fields beyond the schema
dominance_rules.rule: schema and prespecification stability dominate population volume
dominance_rules.required_action: keep prespecified fields and criteria; route additions through amendment
dominance_rules.example: adding extraction fields ad hoc during extraction

dominance_rules.trigger: a comprehensive grey step cannot be documented reproducibly
dominance_rules.rule: documented reproducibility dominates undocumented comprehensiveness in the reporting claim
dominance_rules.required_action: document the step fully or disclose it as a non-reproducible limitation
dominance_rules.example: author-contact searching that cannot be replicated and is undisclosed

dominance_rules.trigger: adding a source improves coverage but raises duplicate and screening cost
dominance_rules.rule: coverage of in-scope disciplines dominates cost until marginal unique yield is negligible
dominance_rules.required_action: add sources until unique yield diminishes, then stop and document
dominance_rules.example: dropping a discipline-essential database to save screening time

dominance_rules.trigger: an object is created without a resolvable source or competency-question link
dominance_rules.required_action: attach a source ref and competency-question link or remove the object
dominance_rules.example: adding a node with no evidence_refs or CQ link

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient sequencing would create a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker dependency to a sequence or feedback edge with a stop condition
dominance_rules.example: making appraisal a hard prerequisite of extraction and vice versa

anti_rework_rules.rule: register and stabilize the protocol before any screening
anti_rework_rules.rationale: screening under an unstable protocol forces re-screening when criteria change
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: screening started before a registry ID exists
anti_rework_rules.example: screening begins with no PROSPERO ID

anti_rework_rules.rule: structure the question before writing eligibility criteria
anti_rework_rules.rationale: criteria not derived from concepts must be rewritten
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: criteria appear before the concept list

anti_rework_rules.rule: finalize eligibility before designing the search
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a search built on unsettled criteria gets re-run
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: search filters change after a criterion changes

anti_rework_rules.rule: peer-review the search before executing it
anti_rework_rules.rationale: running an unreviewed search risks a full re-run and re-screen
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the search was executed with no PRESS report

anti_rework_rules.rationale: an uncalibrated search either misses studies or floods screening
anti_rework_rules.example: search run without a seed-set check

anti_rework_rules.rationale: screening duplicates wastes effort and double-counts
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: screening starts on a non-deduplicated set
anti_rework_rules.example: raw merged records sent to screening

anti_rework_rules.rule: run a screening-calibration exercise before full screening
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: agreement not measured before full screening

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate automation recall before trusting auto-exclusion
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unvalidated auto-exclusion silently drops studies, needing re-screening
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: auto-exclusion used with no recall estimate

anti_rework_rules.rule: confirm the final included set before extraction
anti_rework_rules.rationale: extracting from a non-final set is wasted on later-excluded studies
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: extraction begins before full-text screening ends

anti_rework_rules.rule: pilot the extraction form before full extraction
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an unpiloted form forces re-extraction when fields prove unfit

anti_rework_rules.rule: reconcile the PRISMA flow before final reporting
anti_rework_rules.rationale: retroactive count reconstruction at reporting is error-prone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: flow numbers do not add up at reporting

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or methods review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and downstream impact
action: score defects by risk and coupling
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defects scheduled first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue ordered and no unranked high-risk defect remains

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect may affect locked or downstream artifacts
iteration_protocol.detection: trace edges and dependencies from the defect node
acceptance_tests: all downstream dependents identified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across two passes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is queued for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map the failure type to its repair subsystem
acceptance_tests: each defect has an owner subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator and recompute derived fields
acceptance_tests: no new failures introduced
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: validation passes with no new failures

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a search update changes a node's importance
iteration_protocol.detection: compare posterior delta to the revisit threshold
action: flag nodes over the revisit delta
acceptance_tests: posteriors recomputed for affected nodes
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior deltas below the revisit threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: a dependency cycle or invalid edge is found
iteration_protocol.detection: run the acyclicity and reference checks
acceptance_tests: dependency graph is acyclic and references resolve
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no cycle and no invalid references remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream node changed after a downstream artifact was locked
iteration_protocol.detection: detect upstream change against lock state
acceptance_tests: all affected dependents downgraded
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no locked artifact depends on a changed unvalidated upstream

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk_if_wrong>=0.80 or confidence below the human-review threshold
acceptance_tests: each high-risk node has a decision record
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: all threshold-crossing items have a human decision

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare metrics against the prior version
acceptance_tests: no regression in mandatory metrics
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: regression report shows no mandatory-metric loss

human_review_required_for: unregistered changes to criteria or outcomes
use of auto-exclusion without validated recall
claiming comprehensiveness from a non-reproducible search
hard lock of the review protocol or final report

test_cases.input_summary: does intervention X improve outcome Y
what is known about topic X
evidence summary needed in two weeks
large record set with ML screening
third party cannot reproduce the search

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked protocol or report change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
human_approval_required_for: hard lock of the protocol or final report
